title: The Gilded Asphyxia
briefing:
Detective, we have a messy situation at 'The Vault', a high-security art restoration facility in the docklands. The owner, Elias Thorne, was found flattened underneath a crate containing a priceless marble replica. It looks like a workplace accident—a snapped winch cable—but the scene feels staged.

The facility is locked down. We have six people inside: the staff, a rival dealer, and family members who were present for an unveiling event. The air inside smells thick with chemicals, and the body has already been moved by the time we got the call.

Your job isn't just to find who cut the cable. The Medical Examiner noticed something odd about the lividity. Thorne might have been dead before that crate ever fell. Dig through the paperwork, check the logs, and don't trust the obvious physical trauma. This was a calculated execution disguised as bad luck.

clues: No blood splatter on floor beneath head
entities.label: Victim's Body (Elias Thorne)
entities.content: Subject found crushed beneath a 200kg marble crate. However, lividity suggests the body was moved post-mortem. Lack of active bleeding from the crush injury indicates heart had stopped beating prior to impact.
entities.description: A middle-aged man in a suit, torso crushed by a crate. Face is blueish.

forensicData.value: High concentration of Tetra-V Solvent in lung tissue.

entities.label: Marble Statue Crate
entities.content: Heavy wooden crate containing a marble statue. The winch cable above appears to have been snapped manually using a tool, not natural wear and tear.
entities.description: Splintered wood, heavy iron chains, markings saying 'Fragile'.

entities.label: Chemical Inventory Ledger (The Boring List)
entities.content:
A tedious 40-page log of every chemical drop used in the lab. Rows upon rows of 'Turpentine - 5ml', 'Varnish - 10ml'. 

Page 39 Entry: 'Tetra-V Solvent | 500ml Bottle | Status: Empty | Signed: E.R. | Time: 19:00'. 
Page 40 Entry (Last Line): 'Acetone | 20ml | Signed: S.J. | Time: 21:30'. 

(Contradiction: E.R. logged the bottle as empty/used at 19:00. However, the Victim was seen alive by S1 at 20:00. Autopsy puts TOD at 20:30. Why was the solvent marked used an hour before the murder?)
entities.description: A dusty, dog-eared binder filled with grid paper and handwriting.

forensicData.value: Entry for Tetra-V matches S1 (Elena Rostova)

entities.label: Empty Tetra-V Bottle
entities.content: An industrial solvent bottle. Highly volatile. The label warns that it displaces oxygen rapidly in enclosed spaces.
entities.description: Amber glass bottle with a skull and crossbones label.

forensicData.value: Matches toxins found in Victim's lungs.

entities.label: Gold Cufflink
entities.content: Expensive cufflink found kicked under the table. Suggests a struggle occurred here.
entities.description: Shiny gold cufflink, distinct art deco style.

forensicData.value: Blood belongs to S2 (Julian Vane), not the victim.

entities.label: Security Camera Still 20:15
entities.content: Grainy footage showing Marcus Thorne walking towards the lab where the body was found. He looks angry.
entities.description: Black and white CCTV still, low resolution.

entities.label: Torn Promissory Note
entities.content: A loan agreement between Elias Thorne and Julian Vane. It appears Elias was lending Julian money to cover gambling debts, but with 50% interest.
entities.description: Crisp paper, ripped down the middle.

entities.label: Rag with Chloroform scent
entities.content: A cleaning rag stuffed into the vent to hide it. It is saturated with the same chemical found in the empty bottle.

entities.label: Draft Email
entities.content: Draft: 'I regret to inform you that due to continued insubordination and refusal to modernize techniques, I am terminating Elena Rostova effective tomorrow morning...'
entities.description: Digital screen capture of an email client.

forensicData.value: Opened and read at 20:05. Victim was alive.

entities.label: Blood under Victim's Fingernails
entities.content: Scrapings from under the fingernails indicate he scratched someone before he died.

forensicData.value: Matches S2 (Julian Vane). Suggests they fought, but doesn't prove murder.

clues: System set to 'Recirculate' (preventing fumes from venting)
entities.label: Broken HVAC Control Panel
entities.content: The climate control was tampered with. It was forced into recirculation mode, ensuring the toxic fumes from the Tetra-V would stay in the room and concentrate at floor level.
entities.description: Plastic keypad with a cracked LCD screen.

forensicData.value: Impact consistent with the heavy gold ring worn by S5 (Victor) or blunt object.

entities.label: Restoration Guidelines (Elena's Manifesto)
entities.content: A pamphlet written by Elena. Notes in the margin: 'He is destroying history for profit. He must be stopped before the auction.'

solution.motive: To prevent the victim from firing her and ruining the art (Entity 09 and 12).
solution.reasoning: The victim did not die from the crate crushing him (Entity 01 - no blood flow). He died of chemical asphyxiation (Entity 01 - Toxicology). The murder weapon is the Tetra-V solvent (Entity 04). The 'Boring List' (Entity 03) shows Elena Rostova (S1) signed out the lethal solvent at 19:00, but marked it as 'used/empty'. However, the autopsy places death at 20:30. She used the solvent to soak a rag (Entity 08, found with her hair DNA) and subdue him, then set the HVAC to recirculate (Entity 11) to ensure lethality. Marcus (S3) later broke in and dropped the crate to make it look like an accident, thinking his father was just unconscious or already dead, but the medical evidence proves Elias was dead via chemicals before the physical trauma. Julian (S2) fought Elias earlier (DNA under nails), but left him alive.

suspects.bio: The head restoration artist at The Vault. A perfectionist who viewed the victim's commercialization of art as sacrilege. She has access to all restricted chemicals.
suspects.name: Elena Rostova
suspects.notes: Obsessed with the preservation of the 'Goya' piece. Very calm.
suspects.visualTags: Severe bun hairstyle, chemical burns on fingertips, pristine white lab coat, distinct smell of turpentine, pale skin

suspects.bio: A rival art dealer who was in the building to negotiate a merger. Known for aggressive tactics and mounting gambling debts.
suspects.name: Julian Vane
suspects.notes: Was seen arguing with the victim 20 minutes before death.
suspects.visualTags: High-end bespoke suit, silk handkerchief, nervous facial tic, sweating profusely, gold cufflinks

suspects.bio: The victim's estranged son. Cut out of the will three months ago. Currently unemployed and owes money to loan sharks.
suspects.name: Marcus Thorne
suspects.notes: Claims he was here to beg for money. His knuckles are fresh.
suspects.visualTags: Disheveled vintage leather jacket, grease under fingernails, biker boots, bruised knuckles

suspects.bio: The unpaid intern. She was the last person to log out of the security system. Often berated by the victim publicly.
suspects.name: Sarah Jenkins
suspects.visualTags: Oversized glasses, paint-splattered denim overalls, messy hair, anxious demeanor, holding a sketchbook

suspects.bio: A wealthy private collector. The victim sold him a forgery last year, and Kray found out today.
suspects.name: Victor Kray
suspects.notes: Physical capability is low, but he is vindictive.
suspects.visualTags: Velvet smoking jacket, silver-handled cane, heavy gold rings, tinted prescription sunglasses

suspects.bio: The victim's wife and a renowned vascular surgeon. Their divorce proceedings were turning ugly over the asset division.
suspects.name: Dr. Aris Thorne
suspects.notes: She has the medical knowledge to kill without leaving a trace.
suspects.visualTags: Sharp angular features, surgical precision in dress, monotone voice, icy blue eyes, expensive handbag

visualTheme: Industrial Brutalism, Flickering Fluorescents, Sterile White vs. Grimy Oil, High Contrast Shadows
